summary: This note is a Wikipedia infobox-style summary of the Crown of Aragon, a composite monarchy or confederation of kingdoms ruled by one king that existed from 1162 to 1716. It lists the name in several languages, official and minority languages, religions, monarchs, legislatures, and key conquest and union dates. It also gives the territory's 1443 area and the modern countries that now contain its former lands.
one_line: The Crown of Aragon, a medieval and early modern composite monarchy (1162-1716) spanning territories now in Spain, France, Italy, Greece and beyond.
key_facts: The Crown of Aragon existed from 1162 to 1716.
The Crown of Aragon is described as a composite monarchy, confederation of kingdoms, or individual polities ruled by one king.
Its name is given as Corona d'Aragón in Aragonese, Corona d'Aragó in Catalan, Corona Aragonum in Latin, Corona de Aragón in Spanish, and Aragoiko koroa in Basque.
The official languages of the Crown of Aragon were Aragonese, Catalan and Latin.
The majority religion of the Crown of Aragon was Roman Catholic, with minority religions of Sunni Islam, Sephardic Judaism and Greek Orthodoxy.
The Crown of Aragon was a feudal monarchy subject to pacts.
Petronilla is listed as the first monarch, ruling 1162-1164.
Isabella I and Ferdinand II ruled jointly from 1479 to 1516.
Charles III is listed as the last monarch, ruling 1700-1716.
The union of the Kingdom of Aragon and the County of Barcelona occurred in 1162.
The Kingdom of Majorca was conquered in 1231.
The Kingdom of Valencia was conquered between 1238 and 1245.
The union of Ferdinand II and Isabella I took place on 19 October 1469.
The Nueva Planta decrees were issued in 1716, the year the Crown of Aragon ended.
The Crown of Aragon had an area of 250,000 km² (97,000 sq mi) in 1443.
